messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D medieval castle-city game inspired by *Steel and Flesh* + *Forge of Empires*, with an isekai/reincarnation anime storyline where the player builds a free-form city and conquers the world.
- User prioritizes mechanics working first and is willing to wait for quality; wants an in-browser preview available to inspect.

## Requirements
- 3D game, phone/tablet first with responsive touch UI, safe areas, mouse support.
- Free-form castle/city building "as I want", not a pre-authored castle; Forge of Empires–style upgrades, economy, population, quests/ranks.
- Steel and Flesh–style siege defense, large battles, siege engines, captain/hero command.
- Storyline: reincarnated/isekai anime story where the player conquers the world.
- Short tutorial at game start covering everything.
- War map with region progression, lore, stronger bosses around the map, and dungeons with bosses and collectible loot.
- Premium shop with skins for multiple things, plus a monthly subscription granting gameplay benefits/edge.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them.
- No real payment processing available; premium purchases/subscription should be clearly simulated/demo.

## Decisions
- Title: **STEEL & STONE**.
- Stack: Vite + Three.js (`three@0.180.0`, `vite@7.1.5`), plain JS modules, procedural geometry/audio, no external assets.
- Modes: campaign (8 waves + boss Warlord Gruk), Free Build sandbox, Continue/save via localStorage.
- Grid: 22×22 cells, `CELL = 2.7`; pre-placed keep at `KEEP_I = KEEP_J = 9`, 4×4.
- Isekai premise: protagonist Caelan Ashbourne, last heir of a burned house, retains memories of a modern city-builder life and receives the “Crown System” (explains HUD, quests, ranks, tutorial).
- World campaign: 5 regions mapped onto existing 8 waves:
  - Home Shore (waves 1–2), Greenvale (3–4), Ashen March (5–6), Frostfang Pass (7), Citadel of Gruk (8).
- Dungeons use elite boss encounters launched from the war map, with unique strong bosses, loot (resources + premium Crowns), first-clear exclusive skins, and repeatable reduced loot.
- Premium account data (Crowns, owned skins, equipped skins, subscription expiry) persists separately from campaign saves.
- Premium shop categories: Livery, Roofing, Masonry, Realm Skies, Captain.
- Subscription “The Sovereign’s Oath” benefits: +20% production, +10% tower/siege damage, −25% repair gold cost, +1 quest slot, exclusive Sun King livery, 200 Crowns on activation. Price shown as $4.99/month; activation fully simulated.
- Starting demo Crowns: 320, so shop can be tested without payment.
- Dungeon skins are first-clear rewards only; subscription skin requires active subscription; other skins purchasable with Crowns.

## Work State
### Completed
- Project initialized; dependencies installed; Vite build succeeds.
- Full DOM shell and SVG icon sprite in `index.html`; extensive responsive CSS in `src/style.css`.
- Complete data in `src/defs.js` for structures, resources, enemies, waves, ranks, quests, upgrades, formulas, prologue, regions, chronicles, victory, dungeons, skins, subscription, captain palettes, Crown packs, and 5 dungeon bosses.
- `src/util.js`, `src/fx.js`, `src/audio.js`, `src/world.js`, `src/castle.js`, `src/units.js` implemented.
- `src/game.js`, `src/ui.js`, `src/main.js` implemented and game is runnable.
- Preview running via `start.sh` in tmux session `steel`, served on `http://localhost:3000` (not 3002).
- Playwright Chromium installed; desktop 1440×900 title/build screenshots verified.
- Tested: new campaign start, house placement, wall drag-painting, economy tick, save/continue, camera controls.
- Fixed island top winding so terrain is correctly lit; raised exposure/sun; palette widths; title cinematic camera; missing `closeSelection` call; masonry bonus application.
- Added `#btn-shop`, `#crown-badge`, dynamic `#boss-name-text`, tutorial DOM skeleton, and bound `#btn-map`.
- Added multi-palette `bannerTexture` in `util.js` (blue, red, frost, ember, verdant, sun, rat with unique emblems).
- Added castle skin support: `Castle.skins`, `tintMaterial`, `tintGroup`, `tintWalls`, `recolorBanners`, `applySkins`, `rebuildVisuals`; roof/stone tint sets; banners follow livery; builds/upgrades auto-tint.
- Added world sky themes: `SKY_THEMES` and `world.applySkyTheme(name)` for day, golden, storm, dawn, crow.
- Added captain palettes: Captain build refactored with tintable materials + `Captain.applyPalette`.
- Added `Combat.startDungeon`, `queueEncounter`, `setupEncounter`, `mode`/`dungeon`/`totalEnemies`, non-scaling dungeon bosses, and distinct `onDungeonComplete` callback.
- Game premium account implemented: load/save `steelstone_premium_v1`, Crowns, owned/equipped skins, subscription expiry, purchase/equip/Crown-pack/subscription methods, skin application, subscription bonuses.
- Game campaign integration added: `clearedDungeons`, `regionsClaimed`, `tutorialDone`, region claim rewards (+60 Crowns), dungeon start/complete/finish/retry, dungeon retry/defeat flows.
- Tutorial hooks added in game for place/select/upgrade/map/wave/hero/ability/waveComplete.
- UI partially updated: imports, tutorial step data (9 steps), new elements, bindings, keyboard M/C, dynamic boss name, dungeon phase/progress labels, bonus quest slot, reward claim/chronicle UI, victory VICTORY copy, dungeon-aware defeat modal.

### Active
- UI still needs `showPrologue`, `startTutorial`/`advanceTutorial`/`finishTutorial`/`tutorialEvent`, `showWarMap`, `showShop`, `showDungeonBrief`, `showDungeonComplete`, `updateCrowns`.
- Game needs `showPrologue` call wiring checked (currently `this.ui.showPrologue()` is invoked but UI method not yet implemented).
- CSS for tutorial, prologue/story modal, war map nodes/lines/panel, shop grid/tabs/cards, council/subscription, dungeon briefs/complete, crown badge is not yet added.
- Build has not been re-run since the latest integration edits.

### Blocked
- Build/runtime verification blocked on finishing the missing UI methods and CSS.

## Next Move
1. Implement UI methods: `showPrologue` (story modal then start tutorial), tutorial state machine (`startTutorial`, `renderTutorial`, `tutorialEvent`, `advanceTutorial`, `finishTutorial`), `updateCrowns`.
2. Implement `showWarMap`: region/dungeon nodes, SVG path lines, lore side panel, claim states, march/enter buttons, Crown balance + shop link.
3. Implement `showShop`: category tabs, skin cards with swatches, owned/equipped/buy states, Crown packs, Sovereign’s Oath panel, demo disclaimer.
4. Implement `showDungeonBrief` and `showDungeonComplete`.
5. Add War Map / Crown Vault buttons to pause modal and tutorial entry point; add shop link in title/victory where useful.
6. Add CSS for all new UI (desktop + mobile 390×844), including tutorial card placement and map/shop responsive layouts.
7. Run `npm run build`, reload preview, and verify: prologue → tutorial steps, map/dungeon nodes, dungeon boss fight, loot/first-clear skin, shop buy/equip/subscription effects, region claims, save/continue.
8. Capture desktop and mobile screenshots; tune visual/layout/balance bugs.

## Relevant Files

content.text:
The user has added an important new requirement: the player's castle should be in the open world so anyone can attack on a massive battle scale, and the player can control different troops individually or all at once. This is a significant change from the current wave-defense design where enemies spawn from camps and path to the keep on an island.

We need to incorporate this. Need to think about scope and practical implementation on top of existing game.

Current architecture:
- Island with 22x22 grid, keep, structures, raiders spawn from 3 camps off the island and path to keep.
- Combat class handles enemies, defenders, towers, hero (Captain Aldric), abilities.
- The player builds freely on the island.
- The game is wave-based.

User wants:
1. Castle in open world (not isolated island? The island is already in a sea; "open world" likely means the castle is part of a larger continuous world where battles happen at large scale, not a separate battle arena).
2. Anyone can attack — presumably persistent/continuous threats, not just scripted waves.
3. Massive battle scale — many units, possibly multiple factions/armies.
4. Control troops individually or all at once — selection and command of groups, plus select individual units.

This is a large feature. We need to decide a reasonable implementation that fits the existing code and can be demonstrated. We should not ask clarifying questions (per earlier requirement); make reasonable assumptions and note them.

Let me plan:
- Add an "open world" layer around the island: a larger landmass or connected mainland with roads, enemy warbands roaming, allied patrols, and distant camps. Or interpret as the existing island is part of the open world and enemy warbands can attack from any direction at any time. The key is to make the castle physically located in a continuous world and allow battles at scale.
- Implement a "War Band" system: in build/sandbox state (or a new "world" state), roaming enemy warbands exist in the open world and periodically march toward the castle. The player can initiate battles or defend when attacked.
- Massive scale: add troop units (allied soldiers) that can be recruited, plus enemy armies. Current Combat only spawns raiders and defenders (static garrison archers?). Add a new troop system that supports dozens/hundreds of units using simple meshes/instancing.
- Control: tap a troop to select it, drag/box select multiple, or "Select All" button. Then tap ground to move, tap enemy to attack. Add command UI.
- Need mobile-friendly controls.

Given the existing code, a full RTS troop control system is a substantial addition. But we should implement a solid playable version.

Let me first finish verifying the current state and then design the open-world troop system. Actually, the last test was testing tutorial CSS; the user interrupted with a new feature. We should pivot to this feature, but also ensure the tutorial issue is resolved. The CSS check showed `cardPointer: auto` while tutorial hidden, but hidden means display:none, so no interception. The earlier interception happened when tutorial was visible (opacity 0 but not display none) because modal open. After reload, we can check with modal open and tutorial visible. But since we've reloaded to title, no modal.

We should fix the CSS rule properly regardless. Why didn't the rule apply? It may not have been loaded due to HMR. After reload, with tutorial hidden, can't tell. Let's later test with modal open. But note the rule specificity should work. Maybe the issue was HMR not applying CSS rule. We'll revisit.

Now the main new feature. Let's think about how to integrate with minimal disruption while delivering the requested experience.

### Interpretation & design

"the player castle should be in the open world so that anyone can attack on a massive battle scale where you can control your different troops individually or all troops at once."

I'll implement:

1. **Open-world terrain**: Instead of a lone island, expand the world into a large continuous coastal landmass with the castle on it, connected by roads to the mainland, with enemy warbands roaming. But rebuilding world.js terrain is complex. Alternative: Keep the island but visually connect it to a mainland via a land bridge and add roaming armies on the surrounding plains. The current world is a circular island with water and 3 enemy camps at the edges. We can extend the land ring: add a large outer landmass around the island with fields/forests, and roads leading to distant camps. Actually the island's radius maybe ~46 units (GRID*CELL/2 = 29.7). The camps are at ~42 units. There's water beyond. The world.js builds island top and shoreline. Adding an outer ring landmass might conflict with water. Let's inspect world.js fully to see terrain construction.

2. **Troop system**: Add a `Troops` or extend `Combat` with:
   - Player troops: swordsmen, spearmen, archers, cavalry. Recruited from barracks? Could be free in demo or cost gold/food. Start with a small company.
   - Enemy warbands: roaming groups on the world map, with size scaling.
   - Control: selection (tap unit, box drag, "All" button), move command (tap ground), attack command (tap enemy).
   - Mass battle: dozens of units per side (e.g., up to 150 total) using low-poly meshes with instancing or simple groups. Current enemies are individual Groups with animation; 100+ might be heavy but okay if simplified.
   - Command modes: "All" toggles all player troops; "Squad" selection by drag; individual tap.
   - Auto-fight: units engage nearby enemies when idle.

3. **Open-world attacks**: A world threat meter with roaming warbands. Enemies attack from any direction and can target the castle. Perhaps continuous "world battle" mode that replaces/augments waves:
   - Add a new "Field Battle" mode accessible from the HUD or triggered when a warband reaches the castle.
   - The existing wave system remains as campaign sieges, but now explicitly set in the open world.
   - Maybe treat each wave as a massive open-world battle: enemies spawn from multiple directions, player commands troops, castle towers support. That satisfies "anyone can attack on a massive battle scale" and "castle in the open world." The current waves already spawn from 3 camps. We can increase wave sizes and add troop control. But "anyone can attack" suggests not scripted, but we can add roaming warbands and an "Attack" button for player-initiated battles.

Given time, implement a **Field Army system** integrated into Combat:
- When a wave or dungeon starts, player troops are deployed around the keep.
- Player can select troops individually (tap), by dragging a selection box, or all at once (button / hotkey A).
- Tap ground to move selected troops; tap enemy to focus attack.
- Troops auto-engage enemies in range; archers fire arrows.
- Enemy AI targets castle and troops.
- Add troop recruitment in build mode: a "Muster" panel/button to recruit units with gold/food. Could be via the barracks structure; units persist in the campaign. This is a big system. Maybe simpler: player starts each battle with a company scaled by barracks/garrison, and can recruit during battle using gold? Hmm.

We need to keep scope manageable but deliver. Let's design a compact but real system:

#### Troop model
Create `src/troops.js` with classes:
- `Troop` base: position, hp, damage, speed, range, cooldown, mesh, team, type, target, state.
- Types: `swordsman` (melee, balanced), `spearman` (melee, anti-cavalry/range 1.8), `archer` (ranged 12), `knight` (fast, high damage), `raider` (enemy), `brute` (enemy heavy), `archer_enemy`.
- Player troop roster persists in game state: counts by type, maybe `this.army = {swordsman: 12, archer: 8, knight: 4}`.
- Recruitment: in build mode, a "Muster" button opens a modal to recruit troops using gold+food. Recruited troops add to roster. Cap based on barracks level/population.
- In battle, roster units are deployed near the keep. If they die, they are lost or wounded. After battle, survivors return; casualties reduce roster. Maybe too punishing. For demo, wounded units recover after victory. Keep simple: roster is persistent; in battle, each roster slot spawns a unit; dead units are removed from roster permanently. But then the player can run out. Provide recruit.

Alternatively, treat troops as spawned fresh each battle from "garrison" and not persistent; but user wants control, not necessarily persistence. Persistent adds depth. Let's implement persistence with casualties and easy recruitment.

#### Selection & command
- In Combat, add `selectedTroops = []`, `selectionBox`, methods:
  - `selectTroopAt(worldPoint)`: raycast? Simpler: find nearest troop within a radius in world XZ.
  - `boxSelect(start, end)`: project troops to screen and select those inside rect.
  - `selectAllPlayerTroops()`.
  - `commandMove(point)`: set target for selected troops.
  - `commandAttack(enemy)`: set target.
- Input integration: main.js controls handle pointer events on canvas. Need to inspect how combat tap commands work currently (`game.commandAt` maybe). Search for `pointer` and `commandHero`. We'll integrate into game `onPointerUp` or similar. Let's read main.js controls and game pointer handling.

#### Battle scale
- Increase wave comps? Maybe add "warband" with 40-80 units. For performance, current enemy mesh builder is complex. Could add simpler enemy meshes for troop units. Use shared geometries/materials, low-poly. 100 units should be fine.
- Spawn player troops around keep, enemies from camps. Add allied troops with banners.

#### Open world
- Modify world.js to add outer landmasses around the island: perhaps a large ring/coast with fields and roads. Since the existing island is a circle with radius ~36, water from radius ~37 outward. We can add a distant mainland ring beyond water at radius 60-140 with forests and camps. But the camera range is 520 and fog 150-330. The playable castle remains on the island. To make it "open world," add a land bridge from the island to a mainland shore on the east/north, plus roaming warband camps. The castle is then physically connected to the world. Visually, we can add a large landmass behind/around.
- Simpler: adjust world generation to make a larger continuous terrain with the castle on a peninsula rather than an island. But that risks breaking everything (cells, water, camera). We can add a "mainland" ring and a bridge without changing the island itself.
- Add roads from the island edge to mainland camps, and a "world" feel with distant castles/mountains.

Let's read world.js to see how island and water are built.
I'll add the open-world army layer with troop selection and control. First let me understand the world terrain and input handling.
